questions.q: What is a smoke test, according to this lesson?
options: A complete, exhaustive test suite covering every possible failure mode
A manual code review performed before deployment begins
A quick, basic end-to-end check run immediately after deployment, before real traffic or data, to catch showstopper problems
A load test that simulates maximum production traffic
questions.explain: A smoke test is deliberately quick and basic — it catches showstopper problems, not every possible bug.

questions.q: In this lesson's storage round trip, what does a successful upload from the VM confirm?
options: That the VM's operating system is fully patched
That the storage account has unlimited capacity
That Lesson 9's network path and Lesson 11's identity grant both work
That the application code has no bugs
questions.explain: The upload exercises exactly the network path and identity grant built in the prior two lessons, and nothing else.

questions.q: Why does this lesson also check a service health endpoint, not just the storage round trip?
options: Because curl is required before any CLI command will work
Because reaching storage confirms the network and identity chain, but not that the application itself is running correctly
Because the storage round trip cannot be performed without a health check first
Because health checks replace the need for a storage round trip entirely
questions.explain: An environment can pass the storage round trip while the application process itself still isn't running — the health check catches that.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does skipping the smoke test actually do to the risk it would have caught?
options: It doesn't eliminate the risk — it delays discovery to a worse moment, such as a real user hitting an error in production
It transfers the risk to the storage provider automatically
It eliminates the risk entirely, since the environment was deployed correctly
It has no effect either way on when a problem is discovered
questions.explain: The underlying misconfiguration doesn't go away by skipping the test — it just gets discovered later, at a worse time.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend running the smoke test immediately after deployment, rather than later?
options: Running it later would require rebuilding the entire environment
Storage accounts and buckets expire if not tested within minutes of creation
It's the cheapest time to diagnose a problem, because you still remember exactly what you just built and why
CLI authentication tokens are only valid during the deployment itself
questions.explain: Running the test now, while the deployment is fresh in memory, makes any failure far faster to trace back to its cause.
